description: SpaceMates is a team of designers passionate about making space science engaging and accessible. We combine industrial design, visual storytelling, and hands-on prototyping to create playful learning experiences inspired by NASA's missions and resources. We value creativity, curiosity, and teamwork, and welcome collaborators in science communication, animation, and education.
summary:
AstroMates is a story-driven educational game prototype for children aged 7–12 that turns space science into practical decision-making. Players join a young explorer and his dog, Buddy, on a spacecraft adventure, tackling challenges involving life support, water purification, and space farming.

Guided by smartwatch hints, children inspect system readings, compare possible actions, and discover the consequences of their choices. Feedback and opportunities to retry encourage exploration and thoughtful problem-solving.

Our prototype combines visual storytelling, character design, game interfaces, and mission flows informed by NASA educational and technical resources. Addressing the Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge, AstroMates aims to make space-habitat systems understandable and engaging while encouraging scientific reasoning, responsible resource use, and curiosity about space exploration.
details:
AstroMates is a story-driven educational game prototype for children aged 7–12, developed by SpaceMates for the Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge. It connects scientific knowledge with practical decisions about the systems that support life in space.

The story follows a young boy who dreams of becoming an astronaut and his dog, Buddy. When a mysterious spacecraft pulls them aboard, their adventure introduces challenges involving life support, water recovery, and space farming. Keeping Buddy safe and finding a way home give the player a personal reason to investigate problems and keep learning.

The gameplay follows a consistent learning loop: observe a problem, inspect system readings, compare possible actions, make a decision, and review its consequences. A smartwatch provides visual explanations and progressive hints without immediately revealing the answer. Choices affect the system’s condition, and feedback explains why an action helped or created another problem. Players are encouraged to reconsider and try again.

The mission designs cover three connected areas:

  • Life support: Interpret cabin-pressure and air-quality indicators, distinguish different system faults, and select an appropriate response.
  • Water recovery: Arrange a simplified treatment process, investigate quality warnings, and understand why water requires verification before release.
  • Space farming: Match lighting to a plant experiment’s requirements and restore air circulation around the plants.

The intended benefits are scientific reasoning, problem-solving, and awareness of limited resources. Rather than presenting isolated facts, the experience shows how air, water, energy, and plant-growing conditions contribute to a functioning space habitat.

Our current prototype includes storyboards, interface designs, mission flows, reusable visual assets, and a visual demonstration. Figma supports interface design and prototype assembly.

ChatGPT assisted with narrative drafting, mission refinement, and prompt development, while OpenAI image-generation tools assisted with visual asset production. The team directed the concept, reviewed the material, and assembled the experience.

The project’s creative approach combines an emotionally engaging companion story with scientific troubleshooting. Consistent characters, a recognizable visual identity, and contextual smartwatch guidance connect the missions into one adventure.

Key design considerations include age-appropriate language, readable interfaces, manageable choices, gradual hints, meaningful consequences, and scientific accuracy. NASA educational and technical resources inform the content, with complex processes simplified for the audience. Further development will include playable implementation, testing with children in the target age group, and evaluation of usability and learning outcomes.
